summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported, from private advices from Birmingham, England, that Tom Allen had been ruined by dissipation and had been so badly beaten by a mob at Cork that his life was despaired of.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Saturday Morning, January 28, 1882, page 7.

facts.fact: A private letter from Birmingham, England, said Allen had 'gone to the dogs': dissipation had made him a wreck, and the property he gained in America had vanished
Allen was attacked by a mob of roughs at Cork, Ireland, and so badly cut and bruised that his life was despaired of; welching on his part was said to be the cause
Allen, who had made St. Louis his home for some years, was in England and Ireland around the start of 1882

notes: The report is secondhand, from a private letter, so its facts are rated medium. The same item is the one the headline of article 646 refers to (same page, same column).
